the_platform_verbatim: Institute a moratorium on all new data centers (similar to New York State) until the legislature can pass comprehensive regulation on data center development.

the_new_york_contrast.finding: The platform cites New York as its model, but the two are not alike. VERIFIED against the NY governor's own release (primary, 2026-07-14).
the_new_york_contrast.new_york: HYPERSCALE facilities only, works by pausing state environmental permits for UP TO ONE YEAR, lifts when a Generic Environmental Impact Statement sets standards
the_new_york_contrast.alaska_proposal: ALL new data centers, no size threshold, no time cap, lifts only when the Legislature acts
the_new_york_contrast.honest_reading: The Alaska plank is BROADER than the model it names. This is a policy finding, not a gotcha, and it is the strongest unreported thing in the file.

mandatory_fairness.no_corporate_framing: SIX INDIVIDUALS GAVE. Anthropic the company gave nothing, has published nothing, and the donor's own op-ed states 'The views in this op-ed are his alone and do not represent Anthropic.' Any line implying 'Anthropic funded a candidate' is FACTUALLY FALSE, not merely unfair. Never write 'Anthropic declined to comment' either, nobody reported asking.
mandatory_fairness.legal_and_ordinary: Out-of-state political giving is legal and ordinary. The story is the CONTENT of the plank and the coalition behind it, not impropriety.
mandatory_fairness.dollars_not_donors: ADN says a majority of the MONEY came from the Lower 48. NOT a majority of donors. Do not flatten.
mandatory_fairness.argue_with_what_he_wrote: Thomas's stated reasoning is ENTIRELY about the pace and safety of AI development. He makes NO Alaska energy argument. If the film juxtaposes his quote with the grid, that is THE FILM'S argument and must be signposted.
mandatory_fairness.other_candidates: Do NOT claim rivals have or lack a data-center position. Could not be established.
mandatory_fairness.case_against: The strongest fair case against a blanket moratorium: a North Slope project generates its own power at the gas source rather than competing with households on the constrained Railbelt grid, so the facility a no-threshold moratorium would stop is the one that does not touch a household's bill.
mandatory_fairness.case_for: The strongest fair case for: Alaska is being asked to approve a load bigger than its own grid before it has any statute governing who pays for the power. 500+ comments, fewer than a dozen supportive.
